en: Vimānavatthu: The Mansion of the Man,
Chapter on Well-Placed [Offerings]
11. The Mansion with Well-Placed Pillars “High is this celestial mansion with its jeweled pillars,
extending twelve yojanas all around.”
There are seven hundred magnificent gabled chambers,
beautiful with pillars of beryl and adorned with golden ornaments;
there you eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.
And divine lutes play their sweet melodies; here,
the five strands of sensual pleasure consist of divine tastes,
and women adorned in gold dance.
By what means is this complexion of yours?
By what means do you prosper here?
And by what means do these riches arise for you?
"Whatever is dear to the mind—
this I ask you, O god of great power:
what merit did you perform while being a human being?"
“By what means have you come to possess such blazing majesty,
and why does your complexion illuminate all directions?
That son of the gods, being delighted, [replied:]
Questioned by Moggallāna, he,
being asked the question, explained it—
the fruit of which action this is.
“Having carefully replaced the poorly placed garland and having restored it upon the stupa of the Sugata,
I have become one of great psychic power and great majesty.”
Endowed with divine sensual pleasures,
because of that my complexion is such as this,
and because of that it shines here.
And riches arise for me,
whatever is pleasing to the mind.
I declare this to you, O bhikkhu of great power.
"Whatever I did while born as a human being,
by that I am thus possessed of blazing power,
and my complexion shines forth in all directions."
The *Sunikkhittavimāna* is the eleventh.
The seventh chapter, the *Sunikkhittavagga*. Its summary verse (*uddāna*) is as follows:
Two were poor forest-dwellers:
the hireling and the cowherd Kaṇḍaka;
[and] Anekavaṇṇa, adorned with polished earrings.
The Serīsaka, the Sunikkhitta,
and the third section of men— thus it is declared.
This is the fourth recitation-section (bhāṇavāra).
The Vimānavatthu-pāḷi is finished.
